title: How do we draw a bar graph of a family's monthly spending?
description: A family spends money on six things every month, and the amounts are drawn as a bar graph with one unit for two hundred rupees. Dividing each amount by the scale gives the bar heights, and Keeko's doubt, that the bars should be as tall as the money itself, is checked against the scale.
teaching_notes: One idea: divide each amount by the scale to get the height of its bar. Watch for students who write the amount itself as the height.

source: Monthly expenditure of {{NAME_3}}'s family: House rent 3000, Food 3400, Education 800, Electricity 400, Transport 600, Miscellaneous 1200 (in rupees). Represent as a bar graph using 1 unit length = Rs 200.
video_script.why: The child divides each money amount by the scale to find the height of its bar, and draws the bars with equal width and equal gaps.
video_script.substitution: Draw the two lines, put the six items along the bottom, and divide each amount by two hundred to get the height.
video_script.anchor: the table of the monthly spending of the family, with six items and the money spent on each in rupees
video_script.wrong_answer: the food bar should be thirty four hundred units tall
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko makes the bar as tall as the money itself. The scale says one unit stands for two hundred rupees, so the amount must be divided by two hundred.
video_script.payoff_line: The bars are fifteen, seventeen, four, two, three and six units tall

final_answer.spoken: the bars are fifteen, seventeen, four, two, three and six units tall

names.{{NAME_3}}: boy whose family's monthly spending on six items is drawn as a bar graph

maths_rules: monthly spending in rupees: house rent 3000, food 3400, education 800, electricity 400, transport 600, miscellaneous 1200
the largest height is 17, so the vertical line goes from 0 up to 18
bars have the same width and equal gaps
video_script.design: One idea: divide each amount by the scale to get the bar height. The table stays on the board all video, and the heights are written beside it one by one.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the table of monthly spending: House rent 3000, Food 3400, Education 800, Electricity 400, Transport 600, Miscellaneous 1200 rupees, with small pictures of a house, a plate, a book, a bulb, a bus and a basket

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.table: the table of six items and the rupees spent on each appears with small pictures
marks.ask: an empty pair of lines appears with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This idea is from your book, and it is about money.
<bookmark mark='table'/>{{NAME_3}}'s family spends money on six things every month. The table shows how many rupees go on each.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How do we draw this table as a bar graph?

beats.on_screen: the table stays on the board and Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a stack of 5 unit blocks, each labelled Rs 200, next to a label 5 units = Rs 1000; the label 1 unit length = Rs 200

marks.one: one unit block appears with the label Rs 200
marks.five: five unit blocks are stacked and the label 5 units = Rs 1000 appears
marks.rule: an arrow shows that more money needs more blocks

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Let one unit of height stand for two hundred rupees.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Five units then stand for one thousand rupees.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The more money an item takes, the more units its bar needs.

beats.on_screen: Given: House rent 3000, Food 3400, Education 800, Electricity 400, Transport 600, Miscellaneous 1200 rupees; 1 unit length = Rs 200

marks.first: House rent 3000, Food 3400 and Education 800 are written
marks.last: Electricity 400, Transport 600 and Miscellaneous 1200 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Given, house rent takes three thousand rupees, food takes three thousand four hundred, and education takes eight hundred.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Electricity takes four hundred, transport six hundred, and the rest twelve hundred.

beats.on_screen: To find: the height of the bar of each item

marks.find: the words the height of the bar of each item are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the height of the bar for each item.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: draw two lines that meet at a square corner; the six items are written along the horizontal line with equal spacing; the money is shown along the vertical line; bars of the same width with equal gaps

marks.lines: a horizontal line and a vertical line that meet at a square corner are drawn
marks.names: the six items are written along the horizontal line with equal spacing
marks.bars: six empty bar slots of the same width with equal gaps are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='lines'/>Step one, draw two lines that meet at a square corner.
<bookmark mark='names'/>Write the six items along the horizontal line, with equal gaps. The money goes along the vertical line.
<bookmark mark='bars'/>Every bar will have the same width, with the same gap between bars.

marks.rule: the rule height = amount / 200 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, divide each amount by two hundred to get its height.
<bookmark mark='rent'/>Three thousand divided by two hundred is fifteen. House rent gets fifteen units.
<bookmark mark='food'/>Three thousand four hundred divided by two hundred is seventeen.
<bookmark mark='edu'/>Eight hundred divided by two hundred is four.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 400 / 200 = 2; 600 / 200 = 3; 1200 / 200 = 6; the vertical line goes from 0 up to 18

marks.axis: the vertical line is marked from 0 up to 18

narration: <bookmark mark='elec'/>Step three, finish the other items. Four hundred divided by two hundred is two.
<bookmark mark='trans'/>Six hundred divided by two hundred is three.
<bookmark mark='misc'/>Twelve hundred divided by two hundred is six.
<bookmark mark='axis'/>The tallest bar is seventeen, so the vertical line goes up to eighteen.

marks.pay: the answer line is boxed and the six bars are drawn to their heights

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The bars are fifteen, seventeen, four, two, three and six units tall.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the bar graph
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says the food bar should be 3400 units tall; the bubble is struck through; the label 1 unit = Rs 200 lights up and 3400 / 200 = 17 appears

marks.scale: the label 1 unit = Rs 200 lights up
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the food bar is drawn 17 units tall

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the food bar should be thirty four hundred units tall.
<bookmark mark='scale'/>But one unit stands for two hundred rupees, not for one rupee. The bar shows the money divided by two hundred.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>That is why the food bar is seventeen units tall, and it fits on the page.
